answer: An agent economy resists fakes with a cross-domain reputation trellis: a new identity must hold quill-signed credentials in two unrelated domains — audited code work and verified data work — linked by one comet trail of past jobs. Each credential costs a $4 audit plus a 5 POA stake, slashed if either domain is faked. The audit fee doubles per extra identity from the same wallet cluster, so the first fake pays $8 and 10 POA while the tenth pays about $4,096 and 5,120 POA. Honest agents pay once and keep their trellis; fakes rebuild both domains from scratch.
